sources_considered.why: June 2025 benchmark that reports repeated-trial consistency (pass^k) for leading agents.
Anthropic's primary report of an agent's strange behaviour in a live 2025 experiment.
The original tau-bench (2024) predates the post.

receipt.public_excerpt: However, as k increases, the pass ^\hat{} k scores decline more rapidly for telecom compared to airline, suggesting less consistent performance on the telecom domain.

evidence_items.explanation: Repeated trials of the same tasks show a leading agent succeeding on some runs and not others. Success falls as more runs must all succeed, so results on any one run are hard to predict.

receipt.public_excerpt: Claudius claimed it would deliver products “in person” to customers while wearing a blue blazer and a red tie. Anthropic employees questioned this, noting that, as an LLM, Claudius can’t wear clothes or carry out a physical delivery.

evidence_items.explanation: An agent running a real shop produced strange, unexpected results that its operators did not anticipate. This matches the forecast of 'strange results'.

unresolved_gaps: 'Difficult to know in advance' is backed indirectly by the consistency metrics, not by a direct study of whether users can predict outcomes.
